name: Intraneural Perineurioma

criteria.description: Presence of concentric perineurial cell proliferation forming pseudo-onion bulb structures on nerve biopsy
MRI showing fusiform nerve enlargement with T2 hyperintensity and contrast enhancement localized to affected nerve segment
Progressive, painless, focal motor and sensory neuropathy corresponding to affected nerve distribution
Positive EMA (epithelial membrane antigen) staining of perineurial cells in biopsy specimen

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria (histopathology, imaging, and clinical presentation) must be met for diagnosis.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Differentiation from other nerve sheath tumors and inflammatory neuropathies is critical.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Focal, progressive motor weakness in affected nerve distribution
searchTerms: gradual muscle weakness in nerve area
progressive loss of movement in nerve distribution

pathognomonic.symptomName: Focal sensory loss or paresthesia localized to affected nerve territory
Painless fusiform nerve enlargement palpable along affected nerve
searchTerms: fusiform nerve enlargement felt under skin

common.symptomName: Muscle atrophy in the distribution of the affected nerve
Decreased deep tendon reflexes in affected limb

searchTerms: mild nerve pain or abnormal sensation

common.symptomName: Nerve conduction studies showing reduced amplitude and conduction block

occasional.symptomName: Positive Tinel’s sign over affected nerve
Mild limb swelling adjacent to affected nerve
searchTerms: mild limb puffiness adjacent to nerve

occasional.symptomName: Mild autonomic dysfunction such as altered sweating

rare.symptomName: Secondary joint contractures due to muscle imbalance
searchTerms: contracted joints due to muscle weakness

laboratory: Nerve biopsy showing concentric perineurial cell proliferation
Immunohistochemistry positive for EMA in perineurial cells
imaging: MRI demonstrating fusiform enlargement of peripheral nerve with T2 hyperintensity and contrast enhancement
genetic: No consistent germline genetic mutations identified; somatic NF2 gene alterations reported in some cases
other: Electrophysiological studies showing conduction block and reduced compound muscle action potentials

distinguishingFeatures: Encapsulated tumor with Antoni A and B areas on histology
Usually solitary and well-circumscribed without perineurial proliferation
Absence of localized nerve enlargement with pseudo-onion bulb perineurial proliferation

redFlags: Severe neuropathic pain unresponsive to standard therapy
Signs of malignant transformation such as rapid nerve enlargement or systemic symptoms
references: Adams et al., Intraneural Perineurioma: Clinicopathologic and Molecular Features, Neurology, 2020
Jessen KR, Mirsky R. The repair Schwann cell and its function in regenerating nerves, J Physiol, 2016
